I am sixty-eight years old. I have farmed for fifty years, and I never went to school. I cannot read, but I know my fifteen and a half mu better than anyone. I learned everything from my mother-in-law and from watching what works. If my neighbor Lao Wang gets a good harvest, I copy him. If something fails on his field, I don't touch it.

Last year, my autumn Chinese cabbage gave me almost five thousand jin per mu. I put down three cartloads of manure per mu, then one and a half bags of compound fertilizer — that is seventy-five jin per mu. When the plants started wrapping their heads, I top-dressed with urea, about one bag per mu total. This year urea is over one hundred yuan a bag, and compound fertilizer is even more. It hurts my heart to spend that much. But my nephew's father-in-law tried to save money on his cabbage last year. He used only half a bag of urea. His heads were loose and small, and the dealer paid him almost nothing. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. So I will use the same amount as last year, maybe even a handful more. Better too much than too little.

I plant five mu of autumn Chinese cabbage. That is my main crop. I buy hybrid seeds from the shop in town — thirty yuan for a small packet, enough for one mu. I till with the rotary machine after spreading the manure. I irrigate five times from my well, and I spray four times for cabbage worms and those little green bugs. I expect four thousand eight hundred jin per mu if frost doesn't come early.

For spring cabbage, I keep two mu. Spring heads don't grow as fat, so I use one bag of compound fertilizer and three-quarters of a bag of urea per mu. Water four times, spray three times. Should get about three thousand two hundred jin.

My cotton is three and a half mu. Cotton prices have been bad for two years, so I will not spend too much. One bag of compound fertilizer at planting, half a bag of urea when the yellow flowers open. Cotton needs deep soil, so I plough that plot. I water three times. I spray four times for bollworm — if you skip even one spray, the worms eat every boll. I hope for three hundred jin of seed cotton per mu.

Maize is three mu. I plant hybrid seeds — I buy new ones every year, they grow stronger. One bag of compound at sowing, half a bag of urea when the plants are knee-high. Rotary tillage. Water twice, that is enough for maize. Two sprays for armyworm. Should get six hundred jin of grain per mu, maybe a bit more if the summer rain is good.

Chili is two mu. I save my own seeds from the thick-walled red peppers — I have been saving them for thirty years, they taste good and sell well. I spread manure and one bag of compound fertilizer, then when the fruit sets I add half a bag of urea and some potassium fertilizer. Peppers need a lot of water, so I irrigate five times. Spray four times for mites. I expect two thousand jin of fresh peppers per mu.

At my age, with just me and my husband, working all this land is hard. My back hurts when I bend. I hire my nephew to help with the ploughing and the spraying — I pay him one hundred yuan a day and cook him lunch. But for spreading fertilizer and watering, I do it myself. I have to watch every yuan. If I spend more on fertilizer, I have less to pay for hired labor. But I would rather work harder myself than cut the fertilizer. The soil must eat first, or my family doesn't eat.
